title: Find Common Elements Between Two Arrays
summary: Given two integer arrays nums1 and nums2 of lengths n and m, determine the count of indices i where nums1[i] is found in nums2, and the count of indices i where nums2[i] is found in nums1.
statement: Given two integer arrays nums1 and nums2 of lengths n and m, determine the count of indices i where nums1[i] is found in nums2, and the count of indices i where nums2[i] is found in nums1. Return the results as [answer1,answer2].
constraints: Count elements of nums1 whose value appears anywhere in nums2.
Separately count elements of nums2 whose value appears anywhere in nums1.
Repeated elements count separately in the array being counted.
hints: Membership sets make repeated lookup constant time.
Build one set for each array.
Count original entries from each side whose value belongs to the opposite set.
Iterating the original arrays preserves multiplicity while sets answer only the required existence question.
editorial: Iterating the original arrays preserves multiplicity while sets answer only the required existence question.

tests.explanation: Two nums1 entries equal two, while one nums2 entry appears in nums1, giving [2,1].
Three entries qualify in the first array and four in the second.
